PRIMARY OBJECTIVE
Create a genuinely NEW, LARGE, HIGH-QUALITY creepy survival world based on: the approved visual reference/references; intended BunkerGame survival-horror vision; approved reusable assets in the Asset Library; and existing gameplay contracts that must remain functional.
The finished environment should feel intentionally art-directed rather than procedurally scattered. The player should perceive a believable, large survival landscape, not Roblox Parts on a flat baseplate.

MANDATORY ORCHESTRATION
Muse is Director and must actually orchestrate the established pipeline rather than merely describing it:
MUSE -> QWEN -> MIMO -> ROBLOX ASSISTANT -> BLOXFORGE -> MUSE VISUAL REVIEW.
Muse owns art/world direction, visual standards, composition, rejection/revision and final visual review.
Qwen owns reasoning, reference analysis, world topology, biome/layout and composition reasoning, and technical planning where useful.
MiMo owns execution orchestration and actual coordination of Roblox Assistant and BloxForge tool calls.

BloxForge owns engineering, technical validation, filesystem persistence, Rojo-safe integration, geometry, collision, pivot/orientation, scale, performance, scripts, gameplay integration, QA and Asset Library registration.
Never claim an agent/tool participated unless actually invoked. Record real invocation/session/request IDs whenever available.

REFERENCE-FIRST RULE
Study the approved visual reference BEFORE major composition. Extract terrain language, vegetation density, tree silhouette/spacing, elevation, path language, rock distribution, landmark hierarchy, atmospheric depth, lighting, palette, foreground/midground/background layering, scale relationships, visual noise, negative space and horror/survival mood. The result need not copy literally but must achieve comparable coherence and believability.

ASSET LIBRARY FIRST
Before generating assets inspect the approved BunkerGame Asset Library. Reuse approved assets/families whenever sufficient. For required variations find the closest approved family, use it as visual/reference base when appropriate, generate/edit through the established native workflow, BloxForge technical QA, Muse visual approval, then register approved reusable variants. Never register temporary, rejected, test or broken assets. Prefer small coherent reusable kits over dozens of unnecessary unique assets.

WORLD SCALE
The new world must feel LARGE and support exploration, survival resource gathering, navigation, tension, long sightlines, controlled sightline breaks, landmarks, forest traversal, combat, bunker discovery and future expansion. Do not create a tiny decorative arena around the bunker.

TERRAIN
Create convincing terrain. Avoid obvious rectangular ground slabs, repetitive wedge hills, evenly spaced hills, artificial seams, identical elevation, or a flat world with decorative bumps. Use rolling elevation, ridges, valleys, depressions, natural slopes, berms, terrain occlusion, overlooks, lower traversal corridors, irregular silhouettes, terrain transitions and natural bunker embedment. Terrain must direct exploration. The bunker must feel built into the landscape.

FOREST
Create a believable forest system. No grids, even spacing, identical rotation/scale/species or obvious procedural circles. Use density gradients: dense, medium, sparse transitions, clearings, disturbed vegetation near infrastructure, forest edges, dead/fallen vegetation, natural gaps and silhouette variation. Use multiple approved variants where available and preserve gameplay readability.

GROUND DETAIL
Use restrained coherent grasses, weeds, leaf/debris zones, stones, branches, roots, dirt transitions, disturbed soil, rubble near structures and environmental storytelling. Avoid uniform random scatter; use intentional clusters and patterns.

ROCKS
Use rocks/boulders as terrain language: isolated boulders, clusters, exposed formations, slope reinforcement, path-edge rocks and landmark formations. Avoid obvious repetition; use approved boulder families and variations whenever possible.

LANDMARKS
Create a limited number of strong navigation/story landmarks, potentially abandoned infrastructure, ruined checkpoint, radio/communications structure, farm remnants, utility infrastructure, lookout, damaged road elements, industrial remnants, natural rock landmark or bunker approach structures.

BUNKER
Preserve required bunker gameplay but integrate it naturally into the NEW landscape with anticipation, partial concealment, storytelling, readable entrance, earth embedment, drainage/utilities, disturbed terrain and transition from infrastructure to wilderness. Do not expose it as an isolated object in an empty field.

WILDLIFE
Add restrained inexpensive ambient wildlife where useful: distant deer, birds, silhouettes and movement. Avoid excessive AI/pathfinding; prefer pooling/low-cost behavior.

ATMOSPHERE
Review Lighting, Atmosphere, fog, ColorCorrection, sky, sun direction, shadows, exterior lights, contrast, saturation and distance visibility. Maintain playability while creating survival-horror mood and atmospheric perspective.

GAMEPLAY INTEGRATION
Preserve or correctly integrate canonical player spawning, harvesting/resources, inventory, scrap, farming, processor, bunker interactions, power, zombies/enemy spawning, objectives, navigation, day/night and survival loop. Do not preserve bad composition merely because anchors exist; move/reintegrate anchors safely while preserving contracts.

SCRIPTS
Add/modify source-authored scripts only where genuinely required for ambient wildlife, environmental effects, optimized presentation, world behavior or integration fixes. Maintain server authority where appropriate; avoid unnecessary per-object scripts and prefer centralized/pool systems.

PERFORMANCE
Review descendant/BasePart/MeshPart counts, collisions, anchoring, lights/shadows, particles, sounds, pathfinding, streaming, duplicated geometry and scripts. Optimize intelligently without sacrificing the intended visual quality.

SAFE SOURCE-OF-TRUTH WORKFLOW
Filesystem/Rojo remains persistent source of truth for approved work, but Rojo is not permission to destroy Studio state. Before destructive synchronization inspect changes, preserve recovery evidence, verify source completeness and intended world root, ensure archived rejected world is not promoted and unrelated Studio work is preserved. Never blind-sync. Create physical recovery checkpoints at meaningful milestones.

STUDIO DISCIPLINE
Freshly discover active Roblox Studio when required; never rely blindly on stale IDs. For Play QA: START PLAY -> verify Play -> intended QA -> STOP PLAY -> verify Edit. Never leave Play running. Do filesystem work only after Edit is verified.

VISUAL QA IS MANDATORY
Technical PASS is not visual PASS. Muse must inspect real visual evidence: player-level spawn, major forest, bunker approach, long-distance view, landmark, representative traversal and weak regions. Reject flatness, blockiness, repeated assets, grid placement, unnatural tree spacing, obvious wedges, floating/buried geometry, ugly silhouettes, empty ground, bad scale, clutter, weak composition, bunker/terrain mismatch, bad lighting, insufficient atmospheric depth or prototype appearance. If weak: REJECT, FIX, CAPTURE AGAIN, REVIEW AGAIN. Never manufacture VISUAL_QA=PASS.
